answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: Within 15 minutes. The operator must contact MSHA immediately, without delay, and within 15 minutes once the operator knows or should know that an accident involving a death has occurred.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA immediately and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number once the operator knows or should know of an accident.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: This applies to a death of an individual at the mine.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent. The 0.4 percent increase per 0.1 percent of methane applies only where methane is present, so it does not apply here.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The increase applies only where methane is present in a ventilating current.
claims.quote: Where methane is present in any ventilating current, the percent of incombustible content of such combined dust shall be increased 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The device must be adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Each operator must make available to each underground miner an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Underground evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months. Each drill must be held for each shift at a time other than a shift change and must involve all persons underground.

claims.text: Mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held

claims.text: The drills must be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground.
claims.quote: Be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground;

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties (under § 48.5), with approximately 8 of those hours given at the minesite.

claims.text: Each new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

claims.text: Approximately 8 hours of the training are given at the minesite.
claims.quote: approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 (8-hour time-weighted average) of 90 dBA. This is equivalent to a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.

claims.text: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway. This appears in both 30 CFR 56.9300 and 57.9300. Berms or guardrails are required where a drop-off is deep or steep enough to cause a vehicle to overturn or endanger persons in equipment.

claims.text: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway (surface mines, 56.9300).
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: The same height requirement applies under 57.9300 (underground mines).
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: They are required on roadway banks where a drop-off is of sufficient grade or depth to cause a vehicle to overturn or endanger persons in equipment.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be provided and maintained on the banks of roadways where a drop-off exists of sufficient grade or depth to cause a vehicle to overturn or endanger persons in equipment.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours.

claims.text: Within the refuge alternative, the breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours.
claims.quote: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours,

answers.question: What must a written bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan contain under OSHA?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not cover OSHA's bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan. They only cover MSHA respiratory protection and respirable dust control plan rules.

answers.question: At what depth does OSHA require a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say at what depth OSHA requires a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box. They cover only MSHA mine rules on slopes and shafts, shaft-sinking buckets, ventilation controls, and definitions.

answers.question: What FAA certification does a pilot need to fly a drone over a mine site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say what FAA certification a pilot needs to fly a drone over a mine site.

answers.question: When does a mine need an EPA stormwater discharge permit for runoff from its site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say when a mine needs an EPA stormwater discharge permit. They cover other topics: impoundment design plans, permits for mining under bodies of water, and site-specific hazard training.
